## Summary

[[stripe]] describes four pricing models for recurring subscriptions. Products represent what the business sells. Prices define how much it charges, the currency and the recurring billing period. The May 12 and November 7, 2026 overviews retain the same four models.

## Pricing models

| Model | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Flat rate** | Customers choose a service tier, such as Basic, Starter or Enterprise, at a flat price. |
| **Per-seat** | Each unit represents one user or license. |
| **Tiered** | The unit cost can vary with quantity or usage. Volume-based pricing applies the rate of the tier reached to all units. Graduated pricing calculates the charge for units in each tier and sums the tier charges. |
| **Usage-based** | Customers pay based on use, for example through a fixed fee plus overage, pay as you go or credit burndown. |

Both overview captures use shorthand that pairs quantity with volume-based pricing and usage with graduated pricing. The separately captured [tiered-pricing guide](https://docs.stripe.com/subscriptions/pricing-models/tiered-pricing) supports quantity or usage as tier inputs and distinguishes the two calculations. See [[source-stripe-tiered-pricing]] for the implementation details.

## Dated usage-based route

The May overview linked to the [subscriptions usage-based pricing guide](https://docs.stripe.com/subscriptions/pricing-models/usage-based-pricing.md). The November overview instead links to the [Billing usage-based overview](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/usage-based.md). The separate November destination introduces Metronome and routes readers to Stripe integration, architecture and migration guidance. The retargeted link establishes a documentation route. It leaves migration obligations, eligibility, and the availability or retirement of the May destination unspecified.

products-prices-pricing-models.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/products-prices/pricing-models, old raw lines 6-21 and new raw lines 7-22 describe businesses combining Products to represent what they sell with Prices to define amount, currency and recurring period. Customers can choose a flat-rate service tier, buy per-user or license units, or be billed with tiered or usage-based prices. Usage-based options include fixed fee with overage, pay as you go and credit burndown. Both captures offer design patterns without specifying API setup, eligibility or state transitions. The tiered row pairs volume with quantity and graduated with usage in both dates. The linked tiered guides clarify that tiers can apply to quantity or usage. Volume uses one selected rate for all units, while graduated pricing sums the charges across tiers. The existing source-stripe-recurring-pricing-models.md covers all four patterns but repeats the shorthand at line 21, which warrants clarification. The proposed summary retains the four models and corrects the tier calculation using the linked guides.
